title: The lucky bean and Barney Josephson's jealousy
summary: Josephson rubbed Turner's lucky bean, publicity grew, and Turner flushed it; he had wished to go to California.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x:
So I had a bean I carried I got from a cat in
Kansas City I was carrying around with me, supposed to be a lucky bean.
You rub it and make your wish an' come true. So Barney Josephson's band
...when it would get slow, Barney Josephson walked up to me, said, "Where's
that bean you got? Let me rub that bean." (Laughs). So I let him rub it.
He went away feelin' good, you know. Sure enough, later on that night,
the joint was packed an' jammed.
So, Walter Winchell gotten ahol'...got to mention it, and I hadda...I
was down there for a lucky bean. So New York City was on fire. Ever'body
comin' down there to see Big Joe Turner with his lucky bean. Ever'body
say, "Let me rub it. Let me touch that bean. I need some luck." (Laughs).
I say, "So make a wish and rub the bean. Hold it in your hand
and rub it an' make a wish. It all come true."
Three or four times it worked. And that made it worser.
Did it ever work for you?

Yeah, it works. So, Barney Josephson was still after me 'bout get...get...gettin'...gettin' with all them chicks in the club. So I had a ball with all them dolls. I had women galore. So, finally, he walked to me one night and asked me, after the movie stars had left...didn't pay the bill...so, somehow or other, he brought it up ...came up again...so I took the note out and showed it to him. She signed her name to it.

I said, 'Here! You wanna see somethin'?' Here's what happened. She told me...she told me she wanted to see me and sent her name over here and everything...told me where to meet her at and everything, and I said, 'I went and met her.' And he left me alone forever then. He didn't bother me no more at all. He said, right today, that Joe Turner had all the chicks: 'Never seen a man with so many women.' I was young and dumb and full of fun.

Yeah. I saw that in the article that Whitney Balliett did in The New Yorker. He quotes Barney Josephson as saying that the women would go wild when they came in to see you at the club. What happened to the bean?
I took the bean and flushed it down the toilet. I got so much publicity on it that I got scared myself.
What happened with you? What did you wish for that you got?
Oh, I didn't wish for much. I wished I'd come to California to make a movie. It was a silly idea I had. When I met all them movie stars, they told me to come out here and git in the movies, you know.
